data.one_liner: Dart string formatting with Python-style braces and printf mini-languages.
data.what_it_does: Provides Python-style brace formatting and printf-style functions for Dart strings. It supports positional and named values, Unicode-aware alignment, locale-aware numbers, and custom formatters.
use_when: You need Python-style string formatting or printf equivalents in Dart.
You want advanced numeric padding, alignment, and grouping options without pulling in heavy internationalization packages.
avoid_when: You only need basic string interpolation (which Dart supports natively).
You are relying on legacy 1.6.0 patterns like string extensions or ambient global intl state without passing format configurations.
strengths: High performance with compiled and cached templates.
Supports both Python-style braces and C-style printf mini-languages.
Immutable configuration objects allow thread-safe locale and custom formatter handling.
weaknesses: Error hierarchy is separate from dart:core's FormatException, requiring explicit catch blocks for FormattingException.
Does not include built-in intl locale support out of the box (requires package:format_intl for advanced intl integration).
